presets.name: Lush clean hall
presets.desc: A three-second modulated hall that wraps clean arpeggios without a metallic ring
presets.notes: The README's clean-arpeggio recipe; mod 70 % keeps a long tail smooth, hicut 6 kHz keeps it behind the pick

presets.name: Ducked lead hall
presets.desc: A 2.2 s hall with 40 ms predelay that steps back while the solo plays and blooms in the gaps

refs.why: David Gilmour's solo tone: delay into a moderate hall

presets.notes: Predelay keeps the attack dry and in front; 6 dB ducking stops the tail from washing out high-gain notes

presets.name: Eighties digital hall
presets.desc: A long, slightly grainy period hall with deep chorusing modulation for 80s ballads

refs.why: Lexicon-era big digital hall on synths and guitars
early-digital hall reverbs across the album

presets.notes: Era 80s: reduced bandwidth and converter grain of early digital units; the README's 80s ballad recipe

presets.name: Dark seventies hall
presets.desc: A warm, band-limited early-digital hall whose tail sits low and soft behind the band

refs.why: the Lexicon 224 hall era of late-70s and early-80s records

presets.notes: 70s era runs the tail at 20 kHz with 10-bit input; the wet high shelf at 35 % darkens without shortening the decay

presets.name: Octave shimmer hall
presets.desc: A long hall fed back through an octave-up shifter: each pass climbs into a glowing halo

refs.why: pitch shifter at +1 octave in a feedback loop with a long reverb
the shimmer heard on The Unforgettable Fire

presets.notes: Shimmer 40 % with a 7 s decay: the octave grows audibly over a few seconds; for two voices and glide use gfx-shimmer

presets.name: Endless cloud
presets.desc: A 30-second, heavily diffused cloud that turns any note into a slow drone, ducked under the playing

refs.why: bowed guitar into vast reverb, building walls of sound
endless drones of reverberated guitar and strings

presets.notes: The README's post-rock wall: low cut and bass decay 0.7x keep 30 s of tail from turning into mud

presets.name: Blooming pad
presets.desc: A reverb that fades in behind each note while the pick attack is removed: guitar becomes a pad

refs.why: worship pad guitars: volume-swelled notes into a huge blooming verb

presets.notes: Bloom fades the tail in, swell removes the attacks from the wet: the dry still plays, the pad grows behind it

presets.name: Dripping surf spring
presets.desc: A hard-hit three-spring tank: the splashy drip of surf lead and twang

refs.why: drenched spring reverb on staccato tremolo-picked surf leads

presets.notes: Drive is dwell on Spring: 65 % hits the springs hard for the drip; mix high, as surf players set the tank near the top

presets.name: Amp spring, low
presets.desc: A gentle two-spring amp reverb, short and low in the mix: the built-in combo reverb at 2 or 3
presets.notes: Low dwell avoids the drip: the spring is felt as space, not heard as an effect

presets.name: Dub spring crash
presets.desc: A dark, overdriven spring for dub: rimshots and skanks thrown into a crashing tank

refs.why: spring reverb slams and throws in the dub mix
Black Ark spring reverb alongside the Space Echo

presets.notes: High dwell makes the tank crash on transients; put mix on EXP for throws

presets.name: Reverse wall
presets.desc: Wet-only reverse reverb: every chord swells in backwards and melts, the dry guitar removed

refs.why: Kevin Shields: reverse reverb on an SPX90, no dry guitar signal

presets.notes: Shields says he uses purely the reverb, none of the dry: kill dry on, mix 100 %. Pair with tremolo-arm bends

presets.name: Eighties gated burst
presets.desc: A dense, flat burst cut dead on the eighth note: huge gated drums and stabs

refs.why: compressed room mic gated about a second after each hit
the first gated-drum sound with Padgham and Collins

presets.notes: Played without cymbals, as Padgham asked Collins: the gate closes the burst on the grid. Also works on guitar stabs

presets.name: Air around the amp
presets.desc: Early reflections only, no tail: always-on air and width around a dry amp sim
presets.notes: Ambience is space without a tail: safe on high gain and tight rhythm, where a hall would smear the palm mutes

presets.name: Classic vocal chamber
presets.desc: A warm 1.8 s chamber with a short predelay: the crooner's echo room

refs.why: Capitol Studios' underground echo chambers on his 50s ballads

presets.notes: Chamber: dense early reflections and a smooth tail; low modulation keeps sustained vowels steady in pitch

presets.name: Piano chamber
presets.desc: A 1.5 s chamber with little modulation: space around piano and keys without pitch wobble
presets.notes: The README's keys recipe: low modulation, as chorusing is obvious on sustained piano

presets.name: Vocal plate
presets.desc: A bright 1.4 s plate with 20 ms predelay and low cut: dense sheen behind a lead vocal

refs.why: Abbey Road's EMT 140 plates behind mid-period vocals

presets.notes: Plate gives instant density; low cut 150 Hz and predelay keep consonants clear

presets.name: Snare plate
presets.desc: A one-second bright plate for snare and toms: the classic drum plate
presets.notes: Plate programs were all over 80s drums (Sound On Sound, 2011, on the Lexicon 224); short decay keeps the groove

presets.name: Octave halo plate
presets.desc: A two-second plate with a faint octave shimmer: a glow on clean arpeggios
presets.notes: Shimmer 25 % is a colour, not the subject; the plate's instant density suits picked notes

presets.name: Short soul plate
presets.desc: A short, tight plate low in the mix: lift for funk and soul chops without blurring the groove
presets.notes: Under a second so 16th-note scratches stay percussive

presets.name: Amp in a room
presets.desc: A 0.7 s room with dense early reflections: a dry amp sim sounds miked in a real space
presets.notes: The README's room recipe; works on crunch and high gain where long tails smear

presets.name: Live drum room
presets.desc: A 0.8 s room with strong early reflections: kit ambience for jazz, indie and rock drums
presets.notes: Early reflections at 70 % give the room mic sound; the tail stays short

presets.name: Bass room touch
presets.desc: A half-second room on the highs only: space for bass without smearing the low end
presets.notes: Low cut 250 Hz into the reverb: only the attack and harmonics reverberate
